rq: joint identification of raw language equivalence and latent intervention partition
primary_work: Baumgartner et al., Disentangling Dynamical Systems: Causal Representation Learning Meets Local Sparse Attention, CLeaR 2026
decision: NARROWED BEYOND LOCALLY IDENTIFIABLE DYNAMICAL-SYSTEM PARAMETERS — NOT ADOPTED
reason: Local state-dependent sparse causal structure can already identify latent dynamical-system parameters from raw trajectories up to permutation and componentwise diffeomorphism. Those residual transformations remain semantically material: simultaneous utterance/parameter/interface recoding preserves the complete trajectory and task law, and locally indistinguishable parameters permit different raw-language and target refinements. The audited theorem does not jointly identify raw-language equivalence, target partition, or denotation.
surviving_candidate: After recovering the finest dynamical-parameter partition identifiable from all reachable local state-dependent causal influence graphs, and separately recovering the finest raw-language equivalence supported by legitimate language dynamics, determine whether preregistered cross-system interventions with independently fixed actuator, sensor, order, or metric orientation eliminate every residual parameter permutation and diffeomorphism and thereby jointly identify Q, the residual target partition P, and denotation d without semantic-label leakage.
public_baseline_reproduction: not started; primary paper is public but a paper-specific official implementation was not confirmed. A faithful reproduction would require preregistered equations, domains, commands, dependencies, assets, checksums, direct Q/P/d metrics, resource limits, and three seeds before implementation or execution
